newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's GAZ seeking $80 million credit.
newsitem.headline: Russia's GAZ seeking $80 million credit.

text.p: Russian automaker AO Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod (GAZ) is seeking $80 million in loans to support a $251 million upgrade of its car manufacturing facilities, banking and industry sources said on Thursday.
The loans include $65 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and $15 million from AKB Avtobank of Russia, EBRD spokeswoman Rebecca Hill said.
"It's in the process of negotiations," Hill said, noting that the EBRD's board of directors will decide on December 17 whether to approve the loan.
The funds will buy the main assembly line and sub-assembly lines for a new Volga car starting in 1998, a source close to the project said.
Mannesmann Demag Foerdertechnik AG of German industrial group Mannesmann AG will supply the main assembly line, which will cost roughly $25 million, the source said.
In December 1995, GAZ received credit of $20 million from the EBRD and $5.0 million from Avtobank to build a $38 million painting facility for its Gazelle light truck.
